questions.prompt: Which can an abstract class contain that an interface is not meant to provide?
options: Method signatures that implementing classes must follow
Fields, constructors and shared state
Members that are public
Nothing; the two are identical apart from the keyword
questions.explanation: The differences table says an abstract class can contain fields and constructors and hold shared state, while an interface primarily defines a contract and usually does not hold instance state.

questions.prompt: `A` and `B` are both abstract classes. Can `public class C : A, B` compile?
options: Yes, because abstract classes behave like interfaces
Yes, as long as `C` overrides every abstract member
No, because C# supports single class inheritance; `C` can inherit only one class
No, because a class can never inherit from an abstract class
questions.explanation: C# supports single class inheritance, so a class cannot inherit multiple abstract classes. It can inherit one class and implement multiple interfaces.

source.section: 7. Can a class inherit multiple abstract classes?

questions.prompt: `Pet` is abstract and inherits the abstract class `Animal`, which declares `abstract void MakeSound()`. Which class must implement `MakeSound()`?
options: `Pet`, because it inherits `Animal` directly
Nobody; abstract members never need an implementation
`Animal`, because it declared the method
The first concrete class, such as `Dog : Pet`
questions.explanation: `Pet` does not have to implement `MakeSound()` because it is also abstract. A concrete class like `Dog` must implement all inherited abstract members.

source.section: Abstract Class Inheriting Another Abstract Class

questions.prompt: An abstract class cannot be instantiated. Can it still have a constructor?
options: Yes; its constructor runs when a derived-class object is created
No; constructors are only allowed in concrete classes
Yes, but only a `public` one that callers use with `new`
No; it must use a static factory method instead
questions.explanation: An abstract class can have a constructor, and it runs when a derived-class object is created, as with `Dog(string name) : base(name)`.

source.section: 4. Can an abstract class have a constructor?

questions.prompt: `CreditCardPayment` and `CashPayment` are unrelated classes that both need a `Pay()` capability. What does the note recommend?
options: An abstract base class, because they share state
An interface such as `IPayment`, because different classes need the same capability
Copying `Pay()` into both classes without a shared type
Making one class inherit from the other
questions.explanation: Use an interface when different classes need to follow the same capability; use an abstract class when there is a strong parent-child relationship with shared code or state.
